historical_record.description: The Middleton Motor Car Company reopened here after the earthquake and fire, and carried on until 1911.

A building contract was recorded for a one-storey and basement brick store building, all work, at $5,992. O. R. Thayer was named as architect and L. A. Hinson as contractor. The owner was the D. Breslauer Estate Co.

In the Redevelopment Agency's first acquisition appraisal for Western Addition A-2, delivered in January 1964, the appraiser Maury Holmes put the market value of the property at $50,000, appraising a 3,900-square-foot building then used for glass installation, which the appraiser valued at little more than the land.
